stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A regional archive holds 4,000 recorded folk songs, and 1,200 of them are sea shanties. A folklorist selected 150 of the sea shanties at random and found that 40% of the selected songs repeat their refrain more than 3 times.
choices: Approximately 40% of the sea shanties in the archive repeat their refrain more than 3 times.
Approximately 40% of all the songs in the archive repeat their refrain more than 3 times.
Approximately 60% of the sea shanties in the archive repeat their refrain more than 3 times.
The sea shanties in the archive repeat their refrain an average of approximately 3 times.
explanation: The random sample was drawn only from the 1,200 sea shanties, so the conclusion can apply only to the sea shanties in the archive. Keep the same statistic, hedged: approximately 40% of them repeat their refrain more than 3 times.

B.why: You extended the result to all 4,000 songs, but no songs other than sea shanties were sampled. Ballads, lullabies and other kinds of songs may use refrains very differently.

C.why: 60% is the share of sampled shanties that do NOT repeat their refrain more than 3 times. You reported the complement instead of the share asked about.

D.why: You turned a percent above a threshold into an average. Knowing how many songs pass 3 repetitions does not tell you the mean number of repetitions.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Excavators at a site recovered 6,000 pottery sherds, and 2,400 of them are red-slip ware. The others are plain ware. An archaeologist selected 80 of the red-slip sherds at random and found that 20 of the selected sherds show traces of soot.
choices: Approximately 25% of all the sherds recovered from the site show traces of soot.
Approximately 25% of the plain sherds recovered from the site show traces of soot.
Approximately 20% of the red-slip sherds recovered from the site show traces of soot.
Approximately 25% of the red-slip sherds recovered from the site show traces of soot.
explanation: First convert the count to a percent: $\frac{20}{80} = 0.25$, or 25%. The sample was drawn only from the red-slip sherds, so the conclusion applies only to them: approximately 25% of the red-slip sherds from the site show soot.

A.why: You applied the result to all 6,000 sherds, but the plain-ware sherds were never sampled. The sample can speak only for the red-slip sherds.

B.why: You moved the result over to the plain sherds, which is a group that was never sampled. The 25% figure comes from red-slip sherds and says nothing about plain ware.

C.why: You read 20, the number of sooty sherds, as if it were a percent. Twenty out of 80 is 25%, not 20%.
